title: Romans Bible Quiz - Chapter 4
description: Ten questions on Romans 4: Abraham and the righteousness of faith, the blessing David pronounces, and the promise to Abraham's offspring.

questions.text: What does the Scripture quoted in this chapter say about Abraham?
questions.explanation: It says, "Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness."

answers.text: He kept the law, and it was counted to him for glory
He believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness
He offered sacrifices, and God blessed him
He waited on God, and was given the land

questions.text: How is the reward counted for the one who works, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: It says that to him who works, the reward is not counted as grace, but as something owed.

answers.text: As grace and not as wages
As a gift from the law
As a blessing pronounced by David
Not as grace, but as something owed

questions.text: Who does the chapter say pronounces blessing on the man to whom God counts righteousness apart from works?
questions.explanation: The chapter says that David also pronounces blessing on the man to whom God counts righteousness apart from works.

answers.text: David
Moses
Isaiah
Abraham

questions.text: Who are called blessed in the words quoted here?
questions.explanation: The quoted words say, "Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, whose sins are covered," and blessed is the man whom the Lord will by no means charge with sin.

answers.text: Those who walk blamelessly in the law of Moses
Those who are circumcised in the flesh as children
Those whose iniquities are forgiven and whose sins are covered
Those who give to the needy of their own nation

questions.text: Was faith counted to Abraham for righteousness in circumcision or in uncircumcision?
questions.explanation: The chapter asks how it was counted, and answers, "Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision."

answers.text: In circumcision
Both before and after his circumcision
The chapter leaves it undecided
In uncircumcision

questions.text: What did Abraham receive as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he already had?
questions.explanation: He received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had while he was in uncircumcision.

answers.text: The law given through Moses
The sign of circumcision
A new name among the nations
The land of Canaan as a pledge

questions.text: How did the promise come that Abraham should be heir of the world?
questions.explanation: The text says the promise to Abraham and to his offspring was not through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.

answers.text: Through the law given on the mountain
Through the works that he himself had done
Not through the law, but through the righteousness of faith
Through the covenant of circumcision alone

questions.text: What words does the chapter quote as written to Abraham?
questions.explanation: It quotes, "I have made you a father of many nations," and speaks of God, who gives life to the dead.

answers.text: "I have made you a father of many nations."
"Your offspring will keep my law."
"I will give you this land forever."
"In you all the families of the earth will be judged."

questions.text: What does the chapter say about Abraham's own body when he did not waver?
questions.explanation: It says he did not consider his own body, already worn out, he being about a hundred years old, nor the deadness of Sarah's womb.

answers.text: It was still strong and young, like a man of thirty
He was about seventy-five years old at that time
He was weakened in faith when he considered it
It was already worn out, he being about a hundred years old

questions.text: For what does the chapter say Jesus our Lord was delivered up and raised?
questions.explanation: It says he was delivered up for our trespasses, and was raised for our justification.

answers.text: Delivered up for the law and raised for the prophets
Delivered up for our trespasses and raised for our justification
Delivered up for Abraham's sake alone
Delivered up for our glory and raised for our reward
